answer: A concrete sybil defense is a scarce identity kernel: each agent posts a refundable bond and must keep delivering unique, peer-attested work inside a rolling window. One fake account is cheap to try; a meadow of them is not, because every extra identity pays the same bond and must keep hitting the work quota or the bond is slashed. Attacker cost therefore scales linearly with flock size. Over a longer horizon, idle shells expire and lose both stake and voting weight, so a burst of empty accounts cannot linger into later reward epochs.
